# Control Narrative: Ammonia Screw Compressor C-101

**Document:** Control Narrative, Section [X]: Compressor C-101
**Revision:** A (Draft for Owner / Engineer of Record review)
**PLC:** Allen-Bradley CompactLogix
**HMI:** Engine Room Office

> **Note to reviewers:** This draft adds detail the process information did not specify, such as timers, deadbands, reset behavior, and failure responses. These additions are needed before the integrator can code it and before it can be tested at FAT. Every value that was not supplied is marked **[TBC]** and listed in Section 18 (Open Items). The Owner or Engineer of Record must confirm or replace these values before coding starts. The ammonia detection and emergency shutdown requirements must also be checked against IIAR 2, ASHRAE 15, the applicable fire and mechanical codes, and the local AHJ. Those codes govern if they differ from this narrative.

---

## 1. Scope

This section covers the control, protection, and HMI functions for compressor C-101 and the machine-room ammonia safety functions:

- Start/stop sequencing and the soft starter interface
- Slide valve capacity control on suction pressure
- Load-limiting overrides for motor current, low suction, and discharge temperature
- Compressor alarms and shutdowns
- Ammonia detection (AE-110A/B), emergency exhaust fan EF-201, and main liquid solenoid XV-120
- The hardwired break-glass emergency shutdown
- Start-frequency limiting

## 2. Definitions

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Alarm** | Annunciated at the HMI. Requires operator acknowledgement. Does not stop equipment. |
| **Trip / Shutdown** | Immediate stop of C-101. Latched. Requires the condition to clear plus a manual reset before restart. |
| **Inhibit** | Prevents an action (start or load) while the condition is present. Self-clearing. Not latched. |
| **Running** | Soft starter "Run" feedback is true. |
| **Run Time** | Time elapsed since the Running feedback first went true for the current start. |
| **Bad signal** | Analog input below 3.8 mA or above 20.5 mA continuously for 2 s [TBC], or a module/channel fault. |
| **First-out** | The first trip to occur in a shutdown event. It is held and shown separately from trips that follow it. |

All setpoints, delays, and deadbands in this narrative shall be adjustable parameters, not constants in the code. Section 16 lists their defaults and access levels.

## 3. Equipment and I/O Summary

| Tag | Description | Type | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| PT-101 | Suction pressure | AI 4–20 mA | Range [TBC], suggest −15 to 100 psig (compound) |
| PDT-102 | Oil differential pressure | AI 4–20 mA | Range [TBC], suggest 0–100 psid |
| TT-103 | Discharge temperature | AI 4–20 mA or RTD | Range [TBC], suggest 0–300 °F |
| II-104 | Motor current (CT/transducer) | AI 4–20 mA | Range [TBC]. Motor FLA entered as a parameter. |
| ZT-105 *(assumed tag)* | Slide valve position | AI 4–20 mA | 0–100 %. **Required for unloaded-start permissive.** See OI-1. |
| C-101 Start | Soft starter run command | DO | Maintained while running |
| C-101 Run FB | Soft starter running | DI | |
| C-101 Fault FB | Soft starter fault | DI | |
| C-101 Ready FB | Soft starter ready / no fault | DI | |
| YV-105L *(assumed)* | Slide valve LOAD solenoid | DO | Pulsed |
| YV-105U *(assumed)* | Slide valve UNLOAD solenoid | DO | Pulsed |
| AE-110A / AE-110B | Machine-room NH₃ detectors | AI 4–20 mA (ppm) + relay contacts | Range [TBC], suggest 0–300 ppm for the analog signal |
| AE-110 Fault | Detector / controller trouble | DI (per detector) | |
| EF-201 | Emergency exhaust fan | DO High Speed cmd; DI Running FB | Low-speed/normal operation by others [TBC] |
| XV-120 | Machine-room main liquid solenoid | DO (energize to open) + hardwired | Fail-closed (de-energize to close) |
| HS-ESD *(assumed)* | Break-glass ESD station outside the room | DI monitoring contact (hardwired circuit) | |
| Machine-room alarm horn/strobe (inside) | | DO | |
| Alarm horn/strobe at room entrances (outside) | | DO | Confirm code requirement. See OI-9. |

**Interlock to other compressors:** Section 10 requires a shutdown of "all compressors". Any other compressors in the machine room must be included in the hardwired ESD circuit and must receive a PLC shutdown signal. The list of those compressors is OI-8.

## 4. Operating Modes

The C-101 faceplate on the HMI has a mode selector: **OFF / MANUAL / AUTO**. Operator access is required.

| Mode | Description |
|---|---|
| **OFF** | Compressor stopped and start command blocked. If it is running when OFF is selected, a normal stop is performed (Section 8). |
| **MANUAL** | Operator starts and stops from the HMI. Slide valve is moved by HMI Load/Unload pushbuttons. Each press produces one pulse of the configured width. All overrides (Section 7) and all trips remain active. Manual load is blocked by every load-inhibit condition. |
| **AUTO** | Operator starts and stops from the HMI. The PLC controls the slide valve to hold the suction setpoint (Section 6). Auto start/stop on suction pressure is optional (Section 6.5). |

- Changing mode bumplessly does not move the slide valve.
- Selecting OFF never bypasses the trip logic.
- **No HMI function shall bypass any trip.** Maintenance bypasses, if wanted, are out of scope unless the Owner adds them (OI-12).

## 5. Start Sequence

### 5.1 Start Permissives

All of the following must be true before a start command is accepted. The HMI shall show each permissive with its status, and shall show "Not Ready – [reason]" when any one is false.

1. Mode is MANUAL or AUTO.
2. No C-101 trip is latched (all trips cleared and reset).
3. No machine-room ESD condition is active or latched: break-glass healthy, NH₃ 150 ppm shutdown reset.
4. Soft starter Ready = true and Fault = false.
5. Slide valve position ZT-105 ≤ start-position limit (default 5 % [TBC]). See OI-1.
6. Start-limit counter allows a start (Section 12).
7. PT-101, PDT-102, and TT-103 are not Bad.
8. PT-101 > low suction trip setpoint (2 psig).
9. TT-103 < high discharge temperature trip setpoint (210 °F).
10. Additional package permissives, such as oil heater, oil level, or oil pump running: [TBC] (OI-2).

### 5.2 Start Sequence Steps

1. The operator presses START, or the auto-start condition is met. The PLC logs a start attempt to the start counter (Section 12) and energizes the soft starter Start DO.
2. **Fail-to-start check:** if Run FB is not received within 10 s [TBC], C-101 trips on "Fail to Start".
3. When Run FB goes true, the Run Time timer starts.
4. **Oil differential startup bypass:** for the first **30 s** of Run Time, the PDT-102 low trip and the PDT-102 low alarm are both suppressed. The low alarm is also suppressed because it would otherwise false-alarm during every start.
5. **Load hold at start:** the slide valve is held at minimum for 30 s [TBC] after Run Time starts. During this period no load pulses are permitted in AUTO or MANUAL. This lets oil pressure and the motor settle.
6. When the bypass expires, the PDT-102 low trip and alarm become active, with their normal delays (Section 9). If oil differential has not reached 25 psid by then, the unit trips after the trip delay.
7. When the load hold expires, the compressor is "Running – In Control". In AUTO, capacity control begins. In MANUAL, load pulses are permitted.

### 5.3 Unexpected Loss of Run

If Run FB drops while the Start DO is energized and no stop was commanded, the PLC:

- de-energizes the Start DO,
- latches the trip "Unexpected Stop / Starter Trip", and
- captures the soft starter Fault FB status in the first-out record.

## 6. Capacity Control (AUTO)

### 6.1 Control Variable and Setpoint

- **Controlled variable:** suction pressure PT-101.
- **Setpoint:** default 15.0 psig. Adjustable from 5.0 to 30.0 psig. Supervisor login required.
- The HMI shall reject entries outside 5.0–30.0 psig and shall log each change with the user, time, old value, and new value.

### 6.2 Load/Unload Logic

The slide valve is driven by pulses on the Load (YV-105L) and Unload (YV-105U) outputs.

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| PT-101 > SP + Deadband | Load pulse, repeated every Pulse Interval while the condition persists |
| PT-101 < SP − Deadband | Unload pulse, repeated every Pulse Interval while the condition persists |
| Within deadband | No pulses |

Default parameters [TBC]:

- Deadband: ±0.5 psi
- Pulse On-Time: 0.5 s (range 0.1–5.0 s)
- Pulse Interval (on + off): 5.0 s (range 1–60 s)
- **Proportional pulse option:** if enabled, Pulse On-Time = Base On-Time × (|error| / Deadband), clamped between Minimum On-Time (0.2 s) and Maximum On-Time (2.0 s). Default: disabled.

PT-101 shall be filtered with a first-order filter, time constant 2 s [TBC], for control use only. Trips use the unfiltered value.

### 6.3 Output Rules (Apply in All Modes)

1. Load and Unload outputs shall never be energized at the same time. The code shall interlock them, and each output's pulse logic shall also check the other output.
2. No load pulse is allowed when ZT-105 ≥ 100 % (max-load limit, default 100 % [TBC]).
3. No unload pulse is allowed when ZT-105 ≤ 10 % (minimum-capacity limit). This holds except during a normal stop or a forced unload to the start position (Section 8).
4. Both outputs are off when the compressor is not Running. Exception: OI-2, if an oil pump allows the slide valve to be unloaded while stopped.
5. Any active load inhibit (Section 7) overrides the Section 6.2 load demand. Unload pulses are still allowed.

### 6.4 Interaction with Overrides

Section 7 overrides take priority over suction-pressure control in this order:

1. Forced unload
2. Load inhibit
3. Normal control

### 6.5 Auto Start/Stop on Suction Pressure (Optional, Default Disabled) [TBC, OI-3]

If the Owner enables this:

- **Auto start:** in AUTO and stopped, if PT-101 > SP + Start Offset (default 3 psi) for 60 s, the PLC starts C-101, subject to all permissives and the start limit.
- **Auto stop:** if ZT-105 is at minimum capacity and PT-101 < SP − Stop Offset (default 2 psi) for 300 s, the PLC performs a normal stop.

When auto start is blocked by the start limit, the HMI shall display a "Start Limit Active" alarm.

## 7. Load-Limiting Overrides

These run continuously while the compressor is Running, in both AUTO and MANUAL.

### 7.1 Motor Current Limit (II-104)

FLA is a parameter, Engineer access, in amps from the motor nameplate. The current limit logic is active only after Run Time > 30 s, so that starting current is ignored.

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| II-104 ≥ 95 % FLA | **Load inhibit.** No load pulses. HMI status "Current Limit". |
| II-104 ≥ 98 % FLA for 3 s [TBC] | **Forced unload.** Unload pulse every Pulse Interval until II-104 < 95 % FLA. |
| II-104 < 93 % FLA [TBC] | Load inhibit released (2 % hysteresis) |
| II-104 ≥ 105 % FLA for 10 s [TBC] | Alarm "Motor Current High". Motor overload protection stays in the soft starter. |

- If II-104 is Bad, the PLC raises alarm "Motor Current Signal Fail" and applies a load inhibit until the signal is healthy. The compressor continues to run at its current position.

### 7.2 Low Suction Pressure Override (Recommended) [TBC]

Purpose: to unload before the 2 psig trip is reached.

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| PT-101 ≤ 4.0 psig | Load inhibit |
| PT-101 ≤ 3.0 psig | Forced unload |
| PT-101 > 4.5 psig | Release |

The setpoint entry (Section 6.1) shall not allow SP − Deadband ≤ the load-inhibit value. With the defaults, a 5.0 psig SP and 0.5 psi deadband give 4.5 psig, which is acceptable.

### 7.3 High Discharge Temperature Override (Recommended) [TBC]

| Condition | Action |
|---|---|
| TT-103 ≥ 200 °F | Load inhibit, alarm "Discharge Temp Load Limit" |
| TT-103 < 195 °F | Release |

## 8. Normal Stop

A normal stop is started by any of:

- the operator pressing STOP,
- the mode set to OFF, or
- an auto stop (Section 6.5).

Sequence:

1. Pulse Unload continuously, at the Pulse Interval, until ZT-105 ≤ the start-position limit (5 %), or until the 60 s [TBC] unload timeout expires.
2. De-energize the soft starter Start DO.
3. If the unload timeout expired, raise alarm "Slide Valve Failed to Unload on Stop". The next start will be blocked by permissive 5.1.5 until the valve is unloaded (see OI-1 / OI-2).

**Trips and ESD do not perform the unload sequence.** They de-energize the Start DO immediately.

## 9. Compressor Alarms and Trips

All trips:

- de-energize the Start DO immediately,
- latch,
- record a first-out,
- raise a high-priority HMI alarm, and
- require (a) the condition to clear and (b) a manual reset at the HMI, Operator access [TBC], before restart.

| # | Condition | Setpoint | Delay [TBC] | Bypass | Action |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Oil differential low | PDT-102 < 35 psid | 5 s | First 30 s of Run Time | Alarm. Clears at > 37 psid. |
| T1 | Oil differential low-low | PDT-102 < 25 psid | 2 s | First 30 s of Run Time | **Trip** |
| A2 | Discharge temperature high | TT-103 > 190 °F | 5 s | None | Alarm. Clears at < 185 °F. |
| T2 | Discharge temperature high-high | TT-103 > 210 °F | 2 s | None | **Trip** |
| T3 | Suction pressure low-low | PT-101 < 2.0 psig | 5 s | None (see OI-5) | **Trip** |
| T4 | Fail to start | No Run FB within 10 s of Start | — | — | **Trip** |
| T5 | Unexpected stop / soft starter fault | Run FB lost, or Fault FB true | 0.5 s | — | **Trip** |
| T6 | PT-101 signal fail | Bad | 2 s | None | **Trip** (low suction protection lost) |
| T7 | PDT-102 signal fail | Bad | 2 s | None (also blocks start) | **Trip** |
| T8 | TT-103 signal fail | Bad | 2 s | None | **Trip** |
| T9 | NH₃ high-high (≥ 150 ppm) | Section 10 | — | — | **ESD Trip** |
| T10 | Break-glass ESD | Section 11 | — | — | **ESD Trip** |
| A3 | II-104 signal fail | Bad | 2 s | — | Alarm and load inhibit |
| A4 | ZT-105 signal fail | Bad | 2 s | — | Alarm. Load inhibit. In AUTO, hold position. Start blocked. |
| A5 | Motor current high | ≥ 105 % FLA | 10 s | 30 s at start | Alarm |
| A6 | Start limit active | Section 12 | — | — | Alarm (low priority) |

**Missing protection to confirm (OI-6).** The process information does not list a high discharge pressure trip, high oil temperature, oil filter differential, oil level, or motor winding temperature. A screw compressor package normally needs these. A hardwired mechanical high-pressure cutout independent of the PLC is required by code. That cutout must be wired in series with the soft starter control circuit. The PLC must monitor it as a trip input (first-out "HP Cutout").

## 10. Ammonia Detection and Emergency Response (AE-110A/B)

### 10.1 Voting

The detectors are voted **1oo2**: either AE-110A **or** AE-110B reaching a level triggers the action. No averaging.

### 10.2 Level 1: 25 ppm (either detector)

PLC actions:

1. Raise a high-priority HMI alarm "NH₃ Level 1 – [detector]".
2. Energize the machine-room audible/visual alarm (inside).
3. Command EF-201 to run at **high speed**.
4. If EF-201 Running FB is not received within 15 s [TBC], raise alarm "EF-201 Fail to Start".

Latching and reset:

- EF-201 high speed and the alarm **latch**.
- Release requires (a) both detectors below 25 ppm, minus a reset deadband of 5 ppm [TBC] (i.e. < 20 ppm), and (b) a manual reset at the HMI, Supervisor access.
- Confirm against code. Some codes require emergency ventilation to keep running until manually reset, with no automatic shutoff (OI-9).

Hardwiring: the detector controller's Level 1 relay should also start EF-201 high speed through a hardwired path. This keeps ventilation independent of the PLC [TBC, OI-7].

### 10.3 Level 2: 150 ppm (either detector)

PLC actions:

1. Raise a high-priority HMI alarm "NH₃ Level 2 – COMPRESSOR SHUTDOWN".
2. Stop **all** compressors immediately: C-101 and every compressor on the OI-8 list.
3. **De-energize XV-120** (closes, fail-safe).
4. Keep EF-201 at high speed. **Level 2 shall never stop EF-201.**
5. Energize the alarms at the room entrances (outside), if required (OI-9).

Hardwiring: the detector controller's Level 2 relay contact shall be wired directly into the hardwired ESD circuit (Section 11.2). This stops all compressors and de-energizes XV-120 without depending on the PLC. The PLC actions above are a duplicate and provide indication.

Latching and reset:

- The Level 2 state latches, in both the PLC and the hardwired circuit.
- Reset requires (a) both detectors below 25 ppm [TBC], (b) a manual reset at a hardwired reset button [TBC], and (c) a reset at the HMI, Supervisor access.
- After reset, XV-120 does **not** open automatically. It requires a separate HMI "Open XV-120" command, Supervisor access.
- Compressors do not restart automatically.

### 10.4 Detector Fault / Signal Fail

On detector trouble DI, or analog Bad, for either detector:

- Raise a high-priority alarm "NH₃ Detector [A/B] Fault".
- Command EF-201 high speed, fail-safe [TBC, OI-10].
- If **both** detectors are faulted, the room has no gas detection. Raise the alarm "NO GAS DETECTION – MACHINE ROOM". Whether compressors should shut down in this case is OI-10.

## 11. Emergency Shutdown – Break-Glass Station

### 11.1 Function

Operating the break-glass station outside the machine room shall:

- stop all compressors (C-101 and the OI-8 list), and
- de-energize XV-120.

EF-201 shall **not** be stopped. It continues in its current state. Whether break-glass should also force EF-201 to high speed is OI-11. Code may require a separate emergency ventilation control switch.

### 11.2 Hardwired Implementation

- The break-glass station's NC contacts, in series with the NH₃ Level 2 relay contact, form the hardwired ESD circuit. This circuit:
  - de-energizes the run/control circuit of each compressor starter, independent of the PLC, and
  - de-energizes the XV-120 coil, independent of the PLC DO.
- The circuit shall be fail-safe: a broken wire or loss of control power gives a shutdown.
- A separate contact, or a monitoring relay on the circuit, provides a PLC DI "ESD Active".
- The PLC also removes its own start and XV-120 commands and latches trip T10 with first-out "Break-Glass ESD".

### 11.3 Reset

Reset requires all three of the following:

1. Restore the break-glass station (replace the glass or reset the actuator).
2. Reset the hardwired ESD relay at its reset button [TBC].
3. Reset at the HMI, Supervisor access.

After that, open XV-120 per Section 10.3 and restart compressors manually.

## 12. Start-Frequency Limit (Soft Starter: Max 4 Starts/Hour)

- The PLC keeps a rolling 60-minute record of start **attempts**, meaning every time the Start DO is energized, including failed starts. It uses the timestamps of the last 4 attempts.
- If 4 attempts fall within the last 60 minutes, start is inhibited, and stays inhibited until the oldest timestamp is more than 60 minutes old.
- The HMI shows:
  - starts used in the last 60 min (0–4), and
  - when inhibited, "Start Available In: mm:ss".
- Optional minimum time between starts: default 0 min (disabled) [TBC]. Confirm with the soft starter / motor vendor.
- The timestamps shall be held in retentive tags and based on the controller wall-clock time. After a PLC power cycle or program download, the start record shall **not** be cleared. If the clock cannot be trusted (e.g. after a battery failure), the PLC shall assume 4 starts were used at the moment of power-up (conservative).
- No operator or supervisor override. Engineer-level reset only, logged.

## 13. Instrument and Signal Failure Summary

| Signal | Failure Response |
|---|---|
| PT-101 | Trip T6. Start blocked. |
| PDT-102 | Trip T7. Start blocked. |
| TT-103 | Trip T8. Start blocked. |
| II-104 | Alarm. Load inhibit. |
| ZT-105 | Alarm. Load inhibit. Start blocked. |
| AE-110A/B | Alarm. EF-201 high speed. See Section 10.4. |
| PLC I/O module fault | Each affected point treated as Bad. Output modules configured so outputs go to OFF on fault (de-energized). |
| PLC fault / CPU stop | All DOs de-energize. C-101 stops, XV-120 closes. The hardwired NH₃ and ESD functions remain operational. |

## 14. Power Failure and Restart

- On loss and restoration of power, C-101 remains stopped. All latched trips are retained.
- **Auto-restart after power failure:** optional, default **disabled** [TBC, OI-4]. If enabled:
  - restart only if C-101 was running in AUTO before the outage,
  - no trips are latched,
  - all permissives are satisfied, and
  - the start limit allows it.
  - Restart delay: 60 s [TBC], staggered from the other compressors.
- After power restore, XV-120 returns to its pre-outage commanded state only if no NH₃ Level 2 or ESD is latched. Otherwise it stays closed [TBC].

## 15. HMI Requirements

### 15.1 Displays

**Machine-room overview showing:**
- C-101 status: Stopped / Starting / Running – Load Hold / Running – In Control / Stopping / Tripped
- Mode
- Suction setpoint and PT-101
- Slide valve position
- Motor current as % FLA
- PDT-102 and TT-103
- EF-201 status
- XV-120 status
- NH₃ ppm for each detector
- ESD status

**C-101 faceplate:**
- Start/Stop
- Mode
- Manual load/unload
- Permissives list
- Active override (Current Limit / Low Suction / Discharge Temp)
- Start counter

**Alarm summary:** priority, time of activation/acknowledgement/clear, and first-out display.

**Trends:** PT-101, setpoint, ZT-105, II-104, PDT-102, TT-103, AE-110A/B. Minimum 1 s resolution with 30 days of retention [TBC].

### 15.2 Security Levels

| Level | Allowed Functions |
|---|---|
| **Operator** | Start/Stop, mode, manual load/unload, alarm acknowledge, C-101 trip reset [TBC] |
| **Supervisor** | Suction setpoint (5–30 psig), NH₃/ESD reset, XV-120 open command, EF-201 reset |
| **Engineer** | All alarm/trip setpoints, delays, deadbands, pulse timing, FLA, override limits, start-record reset |

Every change made at Supervisor or Engineer level is logged with user, timestamp, old value, and new value.

Trip setpoints should be range-limited in the code so they cannot be set less safe than the vendor's limits. Values come from the compressor vendor [TBC].

## 17. FAT Test Matrix

**Method.** Analog signals shall be simulated by mA injection at the field terminals, not by forcing tags in the PLC. Discrete inputs shall be simulated by jumpers or switches at the terminals. The soft starter Run/Fault/Ready signals are simulated. Hardwired ESD tests shall be done with the PLC in Program mode or disconnected, to prove the shutdown does not depend on the PLC.

| ID | Ref | Test | Expected Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| F01 | 5.1 | Remove each permissive one at a time and try to start | Start blocked. HMI shows the correct reason. |
| F02 | 5.2 | Normal start, Run FB given at 2 s | Start DO on. Run Time begins. Load hold 30 s. Then "In Control". |
| F03 | 5.2 | Start with no Run FB | Trip T4 at 10 s, first-out shown |
| F04 | 5.2 | Hold PDT-102 at 20 psid from the start | No alarm and no trip before 30 s. Trip T1 at 30 s + 2 s. |
| F05 | 9 | After the bypass, ramp PDT-102 down | Alarm A1 at < 35 psid after 5 s. Trip T1 at < 25 psid after 2 s. |
| F06 | 9 | Ramp TT-103 up | Load inhibit at 200 °F. Alarm A2 at 190 °F. Trip T2 at 210 °F. |
| F07 | 9 | Drop PT-101 | Load inhibit at 4.0. Forced unload at 3.0. Trip T3 at < 2.0 psig after 5 s. |
| F08 | 13 | Open-circuit PT-101, PDT-102, TT-103 (each) | Correct trip T6, T7, or T8 within 2 s |
| F09 | 6.2 | PT-101 = SP + 1 psi | Load pulses of the configured on-time at the configured interval |
| F10 | 6.2 | PT-101 = SP − 1 psi | Unload pulses |
| F11 | 6.2 | PT-101 within the deadband | No pulses |
| F12 | 6.3 | Watch the outputs throughout all tests | Load and Unload never on together |
| F13 | 6.3 | ZT-105 = 100 %, demand load | No load pulse |
| F14 | 6.3 | ZT-105 = 10 %, demand unload, in control | No unload pulse |
| F15 | 7.1 | II-104 at 95 % FLA, demand load | Load inhibited. "Current Limit" shown. |
| F16 | 7.1 | II-104 at 98 % FLA for 3 s | Forced unload pulses until < 95 % |
| F17 | 7.1 | Reduce II-104 to 94 %, then to 92 % | Inhibit stays at 94 %, releases at < 93 % |
| F18 | 7.1 | II-104 at 98 % during the first 30 s | No current-limit action |
| F19 | 7.1 | II-104 open circuit | Alarm A3. Load inhibit. Unit keeps running. |
| F20 | 6.1 | Enter setpoints 4.9, 5.0, 30.0, 30.1 as Operator and as Supervisor | Operator denied. Supervisor: 5.0 and 30.0 accepted, 4.9 and 30.1 rejected. Change logged. |
| F21 | 4 | MANUAL load/unload buttons with an override active | Load blocked when inhibited. Unload allowed. |
| F22 | 8 | Normal stop | Unload to ≤ 5 %, then Start DO off |
| F23 | 8 | Normal stop with ZT-105 stuck | Timeout at 60 s, stop, alarm raised. Next start blocked. |
| F24 | 12 | Do 4 starts and stops quickly; try a 5th | 5th blocked, countdown shown. Allowed when the 1st start is 60 min old (time-accelerated test acceptable with Owner's agreement). |
| F25 | 12 | 4 starts used, then cycle PLC power | Start record retained and still inhibited |
| F26 | 12 | Failed start (F03) counts toward the limit | Counter increments |
| F27 | 10.2 | AE-110A = 25 ppm | Alarm. Room horn/strobe on. EF-201 high-speed command. Repeat for AE-110B. |
